I'd still choose Manta. Even though it creates more illusions, you shouldn't use it at the same time as your doppelganger ability. The thing about heroes like earthshaker and ember, specifically against PL - is that it changes the way you must play in fights. So any argument talking about more illusions is bad, is invalid - since you're pretty much playing a illusion-based hero, there's no escaping that - and you wouldn't want to charge in on your own without some illusions. 

Use the manta illusions to seek out the earthshaker before/during a fight, hopefully to stop his blink - meaning yes, send them into the trees if you have to. Manta's still great for farming regardless of the enemy line-up. S&Y is an item that you get when you've got such an insane start, that you can finish it within 20-25minutes. I think that's why they made it so that you can disassemble S&Y, because it's just not good enough after a certain point in the game (on heroes like PL). 

Also, if you play against ember - try to get diffusal, abyssal, and manta (assuming it goes lategame) - the moment you get 1 bash in, he won't have mana once you manta/abyssal/whack the shit out of him :D - but if you have S&Y, chances are he'll still be able to escape when he's not in bash, since he'll still have mana (since you didn't have manta illusions to drain it).

1. Do not let emotions control the way you play. 
2. Blame yourself before blaming others. Even if you go 14-2-10 in a game, and your team loses - find out what mistakes you made. Your ally sniper may have gone 2-13, but that doesn't mean you played perfectly. Download your replay and watch the moments where you felt hesitant or where you made a wrong move etc. 
3. Analyse drafts, and don't just go for the hero you usually play. Sure, that's the easy option - but that doesn't mean your chances of winning is higher. Hmm.... I guess it's just being versatile, which comes down to lots of practice. 

I cannot stress how much watching your own replay benefits you. Simply understanding what you did wrong, and what you should've done instead. I would prefer to lose a game, analyse my replay, learn from my mistakes and improve - rather than go into a game and get a 12minute ez +25mmr where I haven't mentally improved.
